text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — Dedicated GPU pool 'resv-us-east-1-prod' capacity exceeded. 3 enterprise reservations showing queue growth and throttled allocations. Severity: P1. Paging alice_oncall.
alice_oncall: oncall here, joining bridge now. link: https://meet.redwood/bridge/1834567890
ben-sre: seeing backlog on queue-manager. requests/sec spiked ~3x over baseline, autoscaler at max_instances=48 and failing to provision due to quota errors (403 QuotaExceeded).
carla-support: Support ticket 8542 from AureliaBank shows repeated 502s from /v1/generate, started ~09:04 UTC.
infra-ops: running pool diagnostics now — I see sustained GPU utilization ~98% across all reserved nodes. Some VMs are in 'AttachRequested' state for >2m.
se-rep-amelia: OrchIDBank also reporting timeouts and degraded throughput on their reserved endpoints. This is high-impact.
ben-sre: logs: 
```
[09:05:12] autoscaler: request_scale -> desired: 52, max_allowed: 48, error: quotaExceeded (project-gpu-quota)
[09:06:03] scheduler: attach timeout for session s-8823 (tenant-8823)
[09:06:44] queue: pending_requests: 421, avg_wait_ms: 3200
```
alice_oncall: quick triage: which tenants are heavy? can we identify noisy neighbor?
infra-ops: tenant-8823 shows 150 concurrent sessions, many long-lived streaming sessions. Marking as noisy-candidate.
ben-sre: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) enforce per-tenant concurrency cap on reserved pool for noisy tenants 2) evict longest-running non-enterprise sessions 3) temporarily route enterprise customers to hosted fallback model variant (lower GPU footprint).
pm-jordan: confirm customer SLAs. AureliaBank & OrchIDBank are enterprise-reserved customers — prefer fallback route before eviction where possible.
carla-support: AureliaBank willing to failover to hosted if we coordinate. Patch notes: lower latency but different model version.
infra-ops: applying temporary concurrency cap for tenant-8823 -> cap 20 concurrent. Running: 
```bash
redwood pool update --pool resv-us-east-1-prod --tenant-cap tenant-8823=20 --dry-run=false
```
infra-ops: cap applied, evicting 60 oldest sessions for tenant-8823 now.
ben-sre: after cap + evict: pending_requests dropped to 140, avg_wait_ms -> 1200. Autoscaler still blocked by quota to reach desired nodes. Need cloud quota bump or scale workaround.
alice_oncall: can we spin up spare GPUs in dedicated non-reserved pool and reassign? Risk: cross-tenant mixing. Only okay as short-term emergency with tenant isolation tags.
infra-ops: we have spare capacity in dedi-burst-us-east but it's not attached to reserved routing. I can patch routing to allow enterprise tenants to burst there for 30m. Executing: 
```bash
redwood routing set-fallback --pool resv-us-east-1-prod --fallback dedi-burst-us-east --tenant-filter enterprise=true --ttl 1800
```
infra-ops: fallback enabled. Starting gradual reroute of enterprise reservations -> 20% shift, monitoring.
ben-sre: monitoring metrics: enterprise tail latency improving, pending queue trending down. Still need quota request with cloud team: open ticket CNQ-1122.
pm-jordan: I'll escalate CNQ-1122 to cloud provider contacts now.
carla-support: informing AureliaBank about planned fallback. messaging sent.
se-rep-amelia: OrchIDBank ops ack and prefer fallback for 15min, then we reassess.
ops-grace: taking second-shift oncall at 09:20 UTC, will monitor for next 4 hours. alice_oncall handing off.
alice_oncall: handing over bridge to ops-grace. summary: noisy tenant (tenant-8823) throttled via cap, evicted long sessions, enabled dedi-burst fallback for enterprise, opened quota request CNQ-1122.
ops-grace: acknowledged. will watch autoscaler, re-run evictions if queue grows, and coordinate with cloud for quota. ping me on this thread for urgent updates. :thumbsup:
